threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's a 'nice' cafe if it serves soy lattes. Locals know it's about the vibe, not the menu.
Caught a glimpse of a guy singing to a traffic cone outside the Ritzy – thought it was just late-night madness until he started beatboxing too.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found a flyer for a silent disco at a local laundromat — only in Neukölln do you disco while your clothes spin.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find parties in abandoned buildings where art installations double as DJ booths. You'll never feel more alive in a concrete jungle.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they react when a BART delay is announced—eyes roll, but there's an unspoken acceptance. Newbies panic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in pajamas trying to catch the 27, shouting at the driver like it was a personal betrayal. Classic Tenderloin hustle.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can stroll into the local markets at any hour. Most close by 2 PM for siesta, missing the best local buzz.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with their metros while staring at a map, blissfully unaware of the shortcuts through the winding streets.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it Dalston Junction, not just 'the Junction'. The old timers know it’s just Dalston, innit?
Heard a guy on the 133 insist the driver was in cahoots with his ex because he took a different route. Must've been a long night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a hipster feeding a pigeon a croissant while discussing existentialism with a street artist on the corner of Weserstraße.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only here do you find a late-night kebab joint with its own art gallery upstairs—where local artists showcase pieces amid the smell of grilled meat.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name at least three unofficial street art spots and have a favorite taco truck that’s not on Yelp.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy pull out a saxophone on the 31-Balboa, playing 'Careless Whisper' while everyone paused mid-scroll. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just a party zone, but locals know the quiet corners like Plaça de la Virreina, perfect for a peaceful afternoon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their unfamiliarity with the metro map—still squinting at it like it's a treasure map. They always look a bit lost.
